title: I'm a PPL holder and USC student, and I made my first aviation game
author: MattB4906
selftext:
Hi everyone!



This is my first time posting here.



I'm a USC student and a PPL holder. For a personal project I was pursuing, I decided to develop a small game called "Cleared for Takeoff: Rivals". I developed it with the help of AI, so I want to be upfront about that.



It is a multiplayer (or solo!) competitive game where your aim is to have and manage as many departures as you can to beat your friends (or the AI!).



On the development side, I used Codex and Claude Code to help with implementation, debugging and testing. The app uses React and TypeScript, with Capacitor to package it for iPhone and iPad. I started with a browser version and then worked through the mobile layouts, touch controls, saving and multiplayer.



One thing I learned was how easily an aviation game can become confusing to someone who doesn't know the terminology. Feedback from first-time players led me to split the aircraft controls into smaller steps and remove a lot of text. I also moved taxi routing to the game itself so the player could focus on managing flights and gates. That took several rounds of changes and testing.



It's free, with no ads or in-app purchases:

[https://apps.apple.com/us/app/cleared-for-takeoff-rivals/id6826722649](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/cleared-for-takeoff-rivals/id6826722649)



Since this is my first app, any feedback would be appreciated! If something feels confusing, unrealistic in a way that hurts the game, or simply isn't fun, please tell me. I'd like to keep improving it.



Thank you to anyone who gives it a try!
